groups.title: Abortion
notes: Different phrasing, same conclusion — not a gestational-line compromise. Christians use soul/murder language; secular conservatives do not. Not the left/right abortion triple in hidden-majority-patterns.md.

statements.text: An unborn child still has a soul. Unless the mother's life is at stake, abortion isn't health care. Thou shalt not murder.

Abortion ends a child's life. Maybe there are reasonable exceptions for mother's health and rape, but the overwhelming majority of abortions are done by irresponsible people who simply want an undo button.

groups.title: Markets and provision for the poor
notes: Different reasons, same conclusion. Commonality is the conclusion with neither stewardship nor Hayek attached.

statements.text: Caring for the poor is the church's work. A large welfare state often crowds that out and treats people as clients instead of neighbors.
Free markets create prosperity. A large welfare state traps people in dependence and costs more than it delivers.

I come to this because I think caring for the poor is the church's work, not because I think the market is an idol. Still, markets do generally create prosperity, and I want ordinary people to be able to earn a living and keep more of what they earn. I do not want a larger welfare state as the default way of providing for poor people; private charity and local help, including the church, should do more of that work.

groups.title: LGBT unbundling
notes: Unbundle gay adults from public sexualization and from rushing minors into medical transition. Commonality does not require Christians to affirm same-sex marriage or secular signers to call homosexual acts a sin.

statements.text: Scripture says marriage is between a man and a woman. Gay people are not my enemy, but I do believe that what they're doing is a sin.

Gay adults should be able to marry; they're participating as best they're able in upholding healthy societal norms of monogamy. That is very different from Drag Queen Story Hour, or "Pride" parades where scantily-clad men prance around in broad daylight, or schools treating gender-distressed kids as a medical-transition pipeline; those are destructive.
